about: Island geometry for terrain generation. Every feature carries a source and a confidence. Where a shape was derived rather than sourced, the note says so in capitals. Gaps are listed in docs/DATA-NOTES.md.
attribution: Coastline, roads, tracks, lakes, park boundaries and mine paths: (c) OpenStreetMap contributors, ODbL 1.0, https://www.openstreetmap.org/copyright
Elevation samples: ASTER GDEM v3 (NASA / METI), sampled through https://www.opentopodata.org/
Local placemarks: PLFC public KMZ placemarks in C:/Users/sbt41/githublocal/plfc-community-platform/data/latest-field-data.json

island.name: Minjerribah
island.bbox_note: Order is [min longitude, min latitude, max longitude, max latitude], from the mapped coastline.
island.width_note: The published 11 km is the usual width. The bounding box spans 15.2 km east to west because Point Lookout and the Amity spit push the extremes apart.
island.source: Bounding box and spans computed from the OpenStreetMap coastline in this pack. Area, length, width and maximum elevation https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/North_Stradbroke_Island
island.note: The published maximum of 239 m is not tied to a named peak in any source found. The highest named peak sampled here is Mount Hardgrave at about 228 m. Treat the location of the 239 m point as unknown.

coastline.name: Minjerribah coastline
coastline.traverse: Index 0 is the Point Lookout headland, the easternmost point. From there the ring runs south down the ocean beach past South Gorge and Main Beach to Jumpinpin, around the southern end, north up the western bay shore past Dunwich (Goompi) and Myora to Amity Point (Pulan), then east along Flinders Beach past Adder Rock, Home Beach, Cylinder Beach, Deadmans Beach and Frenchmans Beach back to the headland.
coastline.simplification: Douglas-Peucker. About 6 m tolerance around the northern headlands and Point Lookout, about 45 m along the long beach and bay runs, from 1,393 source vertices.

elevation_grid.name: Island elevation grid
elevation_grid.source: ASTER GDEM v3 (NASA / METI), sampled through https://www.opentopodata.org/. Grid clipped to the OpenStreetMap coastline in this pack.
elevation_grid.note: A surface model, not a ground model: over the eucalypt ridges and the paperbark swamp these values include canopy, so they read high by roughly the height of the trees. Vertical error on ASTER is commonly quoted around 10 to 20 m. Good enough to shape terrain, not good enough to plan drainage. Replace with Queensland LiDAR derived elevation when someone can get it.

water_bodies.name: Blue Lake
water_bodies.outflow: Overflows east into Eighteen Mile Swamp.
water_bodies.source: Geometry https://www.openstreetmap.org/relation/20709286 (ODbL). Area, depth and lake type https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blue_Lake_(Queensland)
water_bodies.note: A window lake, not a perched lake: the island water table surfaces here. Sits inside Naree Budjong Djara National Park. The Quandamooka name is published in both the Kaboora and Karboora spellings; the spelling to use should be confirmed with QYAC. Cultural significance belongs in data/lore.json, not here. The OpenStreetMap outline encloses about 9.2 ha against the published 7.3 ha, so the mapped edge runs wide.

water_bodies.name: Brown Lake
water_bodies.note: Perched above the water table on an organic hardpan. Water is stained by tannins from the surrounding tea trees. Published area figures vary and were not verified, so only the figure computed from the mapped outline is given. Culturally significant to Quandamooka women; that material belongs in data/lore.json with a QYAC source.

water_bodies.name: Tortoise Lagoon
water_bodies.note: Perched lagoon west of Blue Lake, tagged intermittent in OpenStreetMap. Water level swings with rainfall.

water_bodies.name: Swallow Lagoon
water_bodies.note: Small lagoon in the central north of the island. Outline is coarse in OpenStreetMap.

water_bodies.name: Eighteen Mile Swamp
water_bodies.source: Area and description https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/North_Stradbroke_Island . Outline derived in this pack.
water_bodies.note: DERIVED OUTLINE, indicative only. OpenStreetMap has no mapped polygon for the swamp. This corridor is offset inland from the ocean coastline between about 27.47 S and 27.70 S, with the inland edge set so the enclosed area is close to the published 3,000 ha, between about 120 m and 1,420 m behind the beach. Published extent is about 30 square kilometres, the largest swamp of its kind. Replace with Queensland wetland mapping before using it for anything that depends on the true edge.

water_bodies.name: Myora Springs
water_bodies.note: Freshwater springs on the western shore north of Dunwich, in Myora Conservation Park. CONTESTED POINT: data/places.json argues this OpenStreetMap node sits about 1.2 km too far inland for a spring that runs through mangroves into the bay, and prefers the conservation park roadside point near -27.4777, 153.4166. Both are in the repo; a local should settle it. Tagged in OpenStreetMap as an archaeological site as well; anything cultural about this place belongs in data/lore.json with a citable source.

water_bodies.name: Western tidal flats (Myora to Amity banks)
water_bodies.note: The sand and mud banks that dry on a low tide along the western shore between Dunwich and Amity Point. Drives the tide, boating and yabby-bank behaviour on the bay side.

protected_areas.name: Naree Budjong Djara National Park
protected_areas.manager: Queensland Parks and Wildlife Service, jointly managed with the Quandamooka people
protected_areas.source: Geometry https://www.openstreetmap.org/relation/6985481 (ODbL, attributed to the Queensland department of national parks). Area and declaration https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Naree_Budjong_Djara_National_Park
protected_areas.note: Declared 2011 and expanded since, so the 5,240 ha figure and the mapped boundary may both be out of date. The park contains Blue Lake (Kaboora) and much of Eighteen Mile Swamp. The park name is published as meaning "my Mother Earth" in the Quandamooka language; that claim and its source belong in data/lore.json.

vegetation_zones.name: Foredune spinifex
vegetation_zones.note: The sand-binding front line. First thing to go in a big east swell, first thing to come back.

vegetation_zones.name: Casuarina foreshore

rule.position: behind the foredune and along the bay shore

vegetation_zones.note: The she-oaks along the camping grounds and the bay-side foreshore.

vegetation_zones.name: Wallum heath

rule.position: older sand plains and lower dune slopes across the interior

vegetation_zones.note: The wallum is the signature community of the island and much of the interior is in it. Two of the island regional ecosystems are listed as endangered under the Queensland Nature Conservation Act.

vegetation_zones.name: Eucalypt forest and woodland

rule.position: the high old dune ridges through the middle and south

vegetation_zones.note: The most widespread forest on the island, dominated by scribbly gum. Koala and glider country.

vegetation_zones.name: Littoral rainforest pockets

rule.position: small sheltered pockets, largest at Myora Springs

vegetation_zones.note: Only small patches exist. The largest is at Myora Springs on the north-west of the island.

vegetation_zones.name: Mangrove and saltmarsh

rule.position: the western intertidal shore, Dunwich north to Amity and south to Swan Bay

vegetation_zones.note: Mangroves hold the inter-tidal zone along the western side, from single trees up to extensive forest in the south and in Swan Bay. Mosquito and midge source, nursery for the bay fishery.

vegetation_zones.name: Wallum swamp and sedgeland

rule.position: Eighteen Mile Swamp and the low ground behind the eastern beach

vegetation_zones.note: Paperbark and sedge on permanently wet peat. Holds the acid frog habitat and a large part of the island freshwater store.

vegetation_zones.name: Mine path rehabilitation regrowth

rule.position: inside the mapped mine rehabilitation areas

vegetation_zones.note: Regrowth on rehabilitated mine paths does not simply return to the community that was there before; structure and soil feedbacks can push it to a different outcome. Age of regrowth varies across the paths and was not mapped.
